title: Collective Chirped STIRAP in a Pair of Three-Level Atoms: Dressed-Manifold Dynamics and Compensation of the Rydberg-Rydberg Interaction-Induced Detuning
authors: Vladimir V. Malinovsky, Svetlana A. Malinovskaya
abstract: We investigate collective chirped stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) in a pair of identical three-level atoms using a symmetric six-state model. Numerical simulations reveal a pronounced oscillatory dependence of the population transfer to the doubly excited Rydberg state on the peak Rabi frequency, indicating dynamics beyond the conventional single-dark-state description of STIRAP. To identify the underlying mechanism, we develop a dressed-manifold description based on gauge-invariant projections onto nearly degenerate instantaneous dressed manifolds. The analysis demonstrates that the wavefunction remains predominantly confined to a two-dimensional dark manifold while becoming transiently coupled to a neighboring bright manifold during the pulse-overlap interval. We further show that in the dressed-manifold representation, the Rydberg-Rydberg interaction modifies the collective resonance structure while preserving the dark-bright manifold dynamics responsible for the oscillatory transfer; an appropriately chosen frequency chirp compensates the interaction-induced detuning and restores efficient population transfer. This dressed-manifold picture provides a consistent interpretation of oscillatory collective transfer and establishes a framework for controlling adiabatic dynamics in interacting multilevel systems by linearly chirped STIRAP, opening a route toward manifold-based control of Rydberg-mediated quantum gates, correlated-state preparation, and other coherent operations in interacting atomic systems.
summary: This paper analyzes collective STIRAP in interacting pairs of three-level atoms, revealing that the dynamics are governed by coupled dressed manifolds rather than a single dark state. The authors develop a framework showing that while Rydberg-Rydberg interactions shift the resonance, applying a specific frequency chirp can compensate this shift, thereby restoring efficient population transfer and enabling controlled quantum gate operations.
main_problem: The paper investigates collective chirped STIRAP in interacting three-level atoms, focusing on understanding dynamics beyond simple dark-state following and compensating for Rydberg-Rydberg interaction-induced detuning.
main_result: The dynamics are governed by coherent evolution within coupled dressed manifolds, and efficient population transfer can be restored by applying a precisely calculated frequency chirp that compensates the interaction-induced energy shift.
method: The authors use numerical simulations combined with a theoretical dressed-manifold description, projecting the full Hamiltonian onto gauge-invariant subspaces to analyze the coupled dynamics.
model_or_system: The system is a pair of identical three-level ladder-type atoms, modeled by a symmetric six-state subspace. The Hamiltonian includes driving fields (Rabi frequencies) and a repulsive Rydberg-Rydberg interaction term ($V_{RR}$) shifting the doubly excited state.
key_observables: Population transfer to the doubly excited Rydberg state ($P_{33}(t)$), and the oscillatory dependence of this transfer on the peak Rabi frequency.
important_parameters: The interaction strength ($V_{RR}$), the chirp rate ($\alpha$), and the pulse timing relative to the interaction-induced resonance condition.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the rotating-wave approximation and the electric-dipole approximation, assuming the dressed-manifold structure remains robust despite the interaction shift.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of populations, showing suppression of transfer with interaction (zero chirp) and restoration of transfer with the analytically derived chirp.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from setting up the microscopic Hamiltonian for the two-atom system to deriving the effective Hamiltonian in the symmetric subspace. It then develops the dressed-manifold picture to explain the oscillatory dynamics, culminating in the analytical derivation and numerical verification of the chirp required to counteract the interaction-induced detuning.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated, manifold-based control scheme for interacting quantum systems, showing how tailored driving fields (chirps) can counteract intrinsic interactions to maintain coherent quantum operations like STIRAP.
